findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch, get_recent_posts, get_post_with_comments · Public sink: fetch, get_post_with_comments.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch, get_recent_posts, get_post_with_comments · Public sink: fetch, get_post_with_comments

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "health_check" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Use this when checking whether an MCP-compatible client can reach the KimchiSushi server." → after: "Check whether an MCP-compatible client can reach KimchiSushi."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
